case_study_insert.main_stem: Evernorth Renewable Energy (ENR) is a public limited company in the renewable energy and battery-storage sector, employing a workforce of 80. Founded in 2015 by Imogen Kaur, it operates a flat structure with democratic leadership. ENR plans to invest $960,000 in an automated battery-storage assembly line with robotic cell welding, financed by a $600,000 ten-year bank loan and a $360,000 share issue. It has fixed costs of $420,000 a year, a variable cost of $18 a unit and a selling price of $42, and currently produces 70,000 units a year. ENR also faces labour turnover of 12% and a rising defect rate in battery cells, and aims to win more residential storage contracts next year.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Quality and HR Report — Q3 2025: ENR assembled 3,500 battery units last quarter at a defect rate of 3.3%, up from 2.0% a year ago. Complaints about early cell failures rose from 18 to 34 per month, and average installation time is 4.5 days. A survey of 520 installers found that 72% value long-life batteries and 61% would pay $3 more for faster-charging cells. A skills audit shows 22 of 80 staff are not trained on the robotic cell welders; an external welding course costs $1,100 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Evernorth Renewable Energy for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 4.5% to 5.25%, raising the cost of variable-rate business borrowing. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 6.2% from $14.50 to $15.40 per hour from January 2027. (3) Lithium and semiconductor input costs have risen 11.3% year-on-year, while demand for residential battery storage grew 7.1% in the same period.

questions.question_text: ENR is funding part of its assembly-line expansion with a ten-year bank loan. Explain two advantages for ENR of using retained profit instead of the bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Retained profit requires no interest payments or fixed repayments, so ENR keeps the cash that would otherwise service the $600,000 ten-year bank loan. That cash can cover fixed costs of $420,000 a year and the running of the new $960,000 battery-storage line, giving room to reduce the 3.3% defect rate and the 34 monthly complaints before they damage the 70,000-unit output. Every dollar not paid as interest can be spent on the robotic welders or on training the 22 untrained staff.

Point 2: Using retained profit keeps ownership and control with Imogen Kaur's shareholders rather than with a lender, so no bank can impose covenants on how the automated line is run. It also avoids pledging company assets while labour turnover of 12% and a $360,000 share issue already dilute and stretch the business. The survey evidence that 72% of installers value long-life batteries and 61% would pay $3 more shows where internally saved cash can be reinvested, instead of paying interest that competes with the $420,000 fixed costs and the cost of fixing the rising defect rate.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual explanation and analysis applied to ENR and its financing decision.

questions.question_text: ENR is launching its automated battery-storage line. Consider an energy-industry trade exhibition, search-engine advertising, or installer-focused social media and training webinars. Which should ENR choose? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Energy-industry trade exhibition: A stand at a trade exhibition lets ENR demonstrate the new battery line to specialist installers and distributors and build credibility in a technical market. However, stand, travel and staffing costs are high for an 80-employee firm already servicing a $600,000 loan and investing $960,000, and only a limited delegate audience attends, too narrow to support 70,000 units of output. It also does little to address the 3.3% defect rate directly.

Search-engine advertising: Ads shown to people searching for home battery storage reach high-intent buyers and can be tightly budget-controlled, which suits the 72% of surveyed installers who value long-life batteries. The weakness is that text ads cannot demonstrate the faster-charging cells that 61% would pay $3 more for, and cost per click can rise quickly when a $960,000 investment must be justified.

Installer-focused social media and training webinars: Technical posts and live webinars can show the robotic welding process and the improved cell quality to installers directly, answering the 34 monthly complaints about early failures. This is low cost per contact, measurable, and can teach correct installation, which matters because faults may come from the 22 staff still untrained on the welders and from the 12% labour turnover.

Recommendation: ENR should choose installer-focused social media and training webinars. They demonstrate quality, reach the exact buyer and cost far less than a trade stand. The exhibition is rejected as expensive and narrow for a firm servicing a $600,000 loan; search advertising is rejected because it cannot demonstrate a technical product or reduce complaints. Webinars lack exhibition face-to-face contact, so ENR should add a small presence at one regional exhibition once the 3.3% defect rate is under control.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited outline of the promotional options with minimal application to ENR.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed discussion of at least two options in the context of ENR with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed discussion of all three options with a well-justified recommendation explaining why the exhibition and search ads are rejected.

questions.question_text: ENR has labour turnover of 12% and a rising defect rate. Explain two benefits for ENR of using democratic leadership within its flat structure to motivate its production staff.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership gives the 80 employees a real voice in how the 3,500 battery units are assembled, so staff can suggest fixes for the rise from 2.0% to 3.3% defects. In a flat structure, their ideas reach Imogen Kaur quickly without passing through several management layers, raising ownership and job satisfaction and helping to reduce the 12% labour turnover that disrupts the automated line.

Point 2: Consulting staff on shift patterns and welder routines uses the practical knowledge of the 22 workers still to be trained on the robotic welders, so training can be scheduled around production and the $1,100 course is better targeted. Involvement also helps tackle the 34 monthly complaints because assemblers who help set quality checks are more likely to catch faulty cells early. With a $960,000 line to run and a $600,000 loan to service, motivation that lowers turnover protects the 70,000-unit output and keeps the 4.5-day installation promise. Democratic leadership suits a skilled workforce whose ideas improve quality, though final quality standards must still be enforced to bring defects down.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to ENR's turnover, defect rate and training needs.

questions.question_text: ENR wants to cut its 12% labour turnover and 3.3% defect rate. Consider a performance-related bonus or job enrichment through team working. Which should ENR choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
Performance-related bonus: Linking pay to cell quality or output could motivate the 80 staff to push the defect rate back from 3.3% toward 2.0% and shorten the 4.5-day installation time. It is simple to understand, but the insert gives no bonus cost, so its expense cannot be calculated; it would add to fixed costs of $420,000 a year while ENR services a $600,000 loan and funds a $960,000 line. A bonus also pays after faults occur and does not change the repetitive welding work that may be driving 12% turnover.

Job enrichment through team working: Giving assembly staff varied tasks, shared ownership of the robotic welders and involvement in quality checks makes the work more interesting and uses their technical skills. Team inspection can catch the faults behind 34 monthly complaints, and shared responsibility can reduce 12% turnover by addressing its cause. Pairing the 22 untrained staff with experienced colleagues also spreads the $1,100 training more effectively. The drawback is the time needed to organise teams and the need for clear standards in a flat structure.

Decision: ENR should choose job enrichment through team working. It attacks the 12% turnover at source, can lower the 3.3% defect rate and costs little next to a bonus whose size is unstated. The bonus is rejected as an expensive short-term fix that does not remove the repetitiveness behind turnover, though a small bonus could be introduced once quality stabilises. With no stated bonus rate the comparison is qualitative: team working changes the work itself and builds skills, while a bonus only rewards output after the event and competes with $420,000 of fixed costs and the $600,000 loan.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of a bonus and job enrichment with limited application to ENR.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of the benefits and drawbacks of both options in the context of ENR.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both options with a well-justified decision covering turnover, cost, quality and motivation.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how ENR's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $420,000 ÷ ($42 − $18) = $420,000 ÷ $24 = 17,500 units. Answer: break-even output is 17,500 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $42 − $18 = $24. Answer: contribution per unit is $24.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways ENR's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare the 17,500-unit break-even output with 70,000 units produced, giving a margin of safety of 52,500 units, so managers can see how far demand could fall before the $960,000 line stops covering costs.
2. Use the $24 contribution per unit to test the $3 premium that 61% of installers would pay: raising price to $45 gives $27 contribution and cuts break-even to about 15,556 units (420,000 ÷ 27).
3. Average total cost is $24.00 a unit ($420,000 ÷ 70,000 = $6.00 plus $18), below the $42 price, leaving scope to absorb the 11.3% rise in lithium and semiconductor costs without an immediate price rise.
4. Labour productivity is 875 units per worker (70,000 ÷ 80), a benchmark for checking whether the $1,100 welding training and team working lift output even with 12% labour turnover.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 17,500 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $24 | (iii) Four contextual uses: margin of safety of 52,500 units; a $3 premium lifting contribution to $27 and cutting break-even to about 15,556 units; average total cost of $24.00 against the $42 price; labour productivity of 875 units per worker.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method and 1 mark for the accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii); 1 mark for each valid applied use in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate ENR's financial position by calculating the gross profit margin and the profit margin for 2024 and 2025. Has ENR's financial position improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 40.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 45.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 20.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 22.0%
ROCE 2024 = 15.0%
ROCE 2025 = 16.5%

Detailed workings: 2024 revenue 1,200, cost of sales 720, gross profit 480; operating profit 240; capital employed 1,600. 2025 revenue 1,500, cost of sales 825, gross profit 675; operating profit 330; capital employed 2,000. Gross profit ÷ revenue: 480 ÷ 1,200 and 675 ÷ 1,500. Operating profit ÷ revenue: 240 ÷ 1,200 and 330 ÷ 1,500. Operating profit ÷ capital employed: 240 ÷ 1,600 and 330 ÷ 2,000.

Evaluation: Every measure is higher in 2025. The share of revenue left after direct costs rose from 40.0% to 45.0% because revenue grew by 300 while cost of sales rose by only 105, so the battery line is becoming more efficient despite the 3.3% defect rate. The share retained as operating profit also rose, and the return on the 2,000 of capital employed improved, which matters because ENR must service a $600,000 loan and has just raised $360,000 of equity for a $960,000 investment. Interest payable of 38 in 2025 is modest beside operating profit of 330, so financing costs are not undermining the gain. The 12% labour turnover and 34 monthly complaints remain risks that could reverse the trend if quality slips.

Conclusion: ENR's financial position has improved. Both margins and the return on capital are higher, with revenue growing much faster than cost of sales. Management should use the stronger margins to fund welding training and quality checks so that turnover and defects do not erase the improvement.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the two margins for both years with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years, detailed evaluation of revenue, cost, profit and capital trends, and a justified conclusion on whether ENR improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for ENR of introducing robotic cell welding on its battery-storage line.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Robotic welding can make cells more consistent, helping push the defect rate back from 3.3% toward the 2.0% level of a year ago and cutting the 34 monthly complaints about early failures. Combined with the survey finding that 72% of installers value long-life batteries and 61% would pay $3 more for faster-charging cells, better quality can protect the $42 selling price, the $24 contribution per unit and the 70,000-unit output.

Disadvantage: The $960,000 automated line adds capital that must be serviced alongside a $600,000 loan, and the 22 staff not yet trained on the welders need a $1,100 course each before they can work on it. With 12% labour turnover, training investment may be lost when staff leave. The insert gives no figure for robot maintenance or energy use, so the exact cost saving cannot be calculated; only a qualitative comparison with the $18 variable cost is possible. If the robots stop, the 3,500 quarterly units and the 4.5-day installation promise could be disrupted, so quality gains depend on reliable operation and training.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to ENR's survey, defect rate and costs.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the base interest rate rise to 5.25%, the 6.2% minimum wage increase to $15.40 and the 11.3% rise in lithium and semiconductor costs will affect ENR. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.5% to 5.25%): If ENR's $600,000 ten-year bank loan is variable-rate, the extra annual interest is 0.75% × $600,000 = $4,500 a year, shown as 0.0075 × $600,000. This is modest against $420,000 of fixed costs, and if the loan is fixed the direct cost is zero. Higher rates may still slow the 7.1% growth in residential battery demand.

Minimum wage increase (6.2% to $15.40 an hour): The insert gives no hours worked or current pay, so an annual wage cost cannot be invented. The derived measure is productivity: 70,000 units ÷ 80 workers = 875 units per worker. If that holds, the wage rise can be absorbed; if the 12% labour turnover and 3.3% defect rate reduce effective output, unit labour costs rise and the $24 contribution falls. The direction is clear but the size cannot be quantified here.

Input-cost inflation (11.3%): The $18 variable cost is not split into components, so an explicit upper bound is 11.3% × $18 = $2.034, about $2.03 per unit. Across 70,000 units that is 70,000 × $2.03 = $142,100 a year. Even a smaller rise cuts contribution from $24 toward about $21.97 and pushes the break-even output above 17,500 units.

Conclusion: The 11.3% rise in lithium and semiconductor costs will have the greatest impact. It applies to every one of the 70,000 units and directly erodes the $24 contribution that must cover $420,000 fixed costs and service the $600,000 loan, whereas the interest rise is about $4,500 and the wage effect is unquantifiable and partly offset by productivity. ENR can recover part of it through the $3 premium that 61% of installers accept, but that premium may not cover a cost rise of roughly $142,100 a year.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external factors with limited application to ENR.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on ENR's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three changes with shown derivations from insert figures and a well-justified greatest-impact judgement.
